Answer: C
Reason: The combination of a large homogenous opacity in the left lung field with fever and, crucially, a discharging abscess on the anterior chest wall is highly characteristic of an infected extralobar pulmonary sequestration that has formed a fistula to the skin (empyema necessitans). Intralobar sequestrations typically present later in life and drain into the bronchial tree, while pneumonia or TB do not typically present with this specific congenital-appearing mass and chest wall sinus tract combination in an infant.
